feedback.problem: Find the range of the function $f(x)=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})-1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The range of $\operatorname{csc}⁡x$ consists of two intervals:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡x\in (-\infty ,-1]\cup [1,\infty )
$$

Horizontal shifts and stretches have no effect on the range. Therefore,

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})\in (-\infty ,-1]\cup [1,\infty ).
$$

We can split this into two inequalities:

$$
\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})\le -1,\,\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})\ge 1
$$

To find the range of $f(x),$ we consider both intervals separately.

- Multiplying the first interval by $\frac{1}{3}$ and subtracting $1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})\le -1 \\  & \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})\le -\frac{1}{3} \\  & \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})-1\le -\frac{1}{3}-1 \\  & f(x)\le -\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

- Multiplying the second interval by $\frac{1}{3}$ and subtracting $1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})\ge 1 \\  & \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})\ge \frac{1}{3} \\  & \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{csc}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{8})-1\ge \frac{1}{3}-1 \\  & f(x)\ge -\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Combining both inequalities, we get

$$
f(x)\le -\frac{4}{3},\,f(x)\ge -\frac{2}{3}.
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the range is $f(x)\in (-\infty ,-\frac{4}{3}]\cup [-\frac{2}{3},\infty ).$
